global_copy.title: Adrian Enev | Full-Stack Developer
global_copy.description: Websites, applications and technical systems by Adrian Enev. Explore business website case studies, mobile development and quantitative research.
global_copy.hero: I’m Adrian Enev. I design and build websites and applications around clear customer journeys, useful interactions and the systems behind them.
global_copy.work_intro: Ten independent website builds, each with a defined audience, a distinct brand identity and a working browser workflow.
global_copy.work_scope: Independent work by Adrian Enev. Business information is illustrative; the case studies document the delivered frontend scope.
global_copy.catalog_heading: Businesses with a clear digital purpose.
global_copy.catalog_intro: Explore the offer, customer journey and frontend work behind each website. Every case study identifies what I built and what the delivered experience does.
global_copy.lab_intro: Software work across IP intelligence, live broadcasting, fitness and quantitative research. Each case study explains the product purpose and my contribution.
global_copy.about: I’m Adrian Enev, a Full-Stack Developer based between Dobrich and Varna, Bulgaria. My work spans website design, web and mobile applications, backend systems and algorithmic research.
global_copy.about_second: I’m studying at Nikola Vaptsarov Naval Academy in Varna. I connect interface decisions with application logic, and use quantitative market research to examine data, backtesting and risk assumptions.
global_copy.contact: Tell me what you’re building, who it needs to serve and where you need help. I welcome project enquiries, internships and technical collaboration.
global_copy.ui_intro: I designed a working study of typography, spatial rhythm and motion. Switch between three states to compare how each decision changes the screen.

ui_modes.type: A large heading establishes hierarchy; supporting details stay secondary.
ui_modes.rhythm: Offset cards and a shifted background change the balance of the composition.
ui_modes.motion: The cards, shape and arrow respond when the selected state changes.

projects.name: Slow Morning House
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A boutique hotel website with room comparison, guest-capacity checks and a stay estimate including optional breakfast.
projects.intro: Slow Morning House is a boutique hotel brand built around considered rooms and a quieter city stay. I designed and developed its website to connect room comparison with dates, guest count, optional breakfast and a sample stay estimate.
projects.customer: Travellers comparing rooms and planning a stay for a specific group and date range.
projects.problem: Guests need to compare room capacity, stay length and extras before choosing the right accommodation.
projects.offer: Three room options, date and guest inputs, room comparison, capacity feedback, optional breakfast and calculated sample totals.
projects.model: The hotel model shown is room-night pricing with an optional breakfast add-on. The build supports stay planning with sample rates.
projects.goal: Make room selection and the estimated cost of a stay easy to understand.
projects.work: I created the hotel identity, responsive room presentation, stay planner, date validation, guest-capacity feedback and pricing calculations.
projects.solution: Room characteristics and planner inputs share one estimate, making the effect of nights, guests and breakfast visible.
projects.outcome: A working three-room comparison and stay calculator with validation and capacity feedback. It does not check live availability or create reservations.
projects.identity: Centered hotel typography, soft blue architectural framing and postcard-like composition position the brand around an unhurried stay.
missing: Provide confirmed rooms, amenities, hotel location, rates, fees and policies before describing a real accommodation offer.
Confirm availability and reservation integration before claiming bookable rooms.
projects.hero: A boutique city stay with room to slow down. Compare rooms and plan dates, guests and breakfast in one stay estimate.
projects.perception: Hospitality slogans describe a feeling, but the portfolio underplays the working room comparison and pricing logic.
projects.edits: Explain the three-room comparison and nights, guests and breakfast calculations. Use Stay planner, keep sample rates and distinguish capacity feedback from live availability.

projects.name: Good Neighbour Homes
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A property website combining home profiles, budget and area filters, saved shortlists and side-by-side comparison.
projects.intro: Good Neighbour Homes is a residential property brand organised around finding and comparing homes. I designed and developed a search experience that connects detailed listings, budget and area filters, a saved shortlist and a comparison view.
projects.customer: Homebuyers narrowing a search by location, property type, budget and practical living requirements.
projects.problem: Comparing listings across separate pages makes it harder to remember trade-offs in price, space and location.
projects.offer: Illustrative home profiles and detail dialogs, area/type/budget filters, list and map views, locally saved homes and comparison of up to three properties.
projects.model: The agency model shown is property discovery leading toward a viewing enquiry. The build covers search and comparison with sample listings.
projects.goal: Help buyers narrow options and compare the details that matter before a viewing.
projects.work: I built the blue and white property identity, listing views, filters, detail dialogs, local-storage shortlist, comparison table and arithmetic budget estimator.
projects.solution: One set of listing data feeds browsing, saved homes and comparison, keeping the decision process connected.
projects.outcome: Working filters, property details, an illustrative map, saved shortlists and comparison of up to three homes. Listings are sample data; there is no listing feed or viewing pipeline.
projects.identity: Clear wayfinding, prominent search tools and readable property cards position the brand around transparent decision-making.
missing: Provide approved listings, listing rights, real prices, agency details and enquiry contacts before representing available properties.
Confirm an actual listing feed and viewing/enquiry integration before describing the website as an operating property portal.
projects.hero: Find a home by area, type and budget. Review the details, save a shortlist and compare the spaces that fit your next move.
projects.perception: The brand promises a calmer search, but the portfolio does not explain its connected filters, saved data and comparison workflow.
projects.edits: Explain filters, persistent shortlists and comparison of up to three homes. Keep listing and map data illustrative, and distinguish the estimator from a property appraisal.

projects.name: Root Ritual
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A hair-care website presenting three oil products and a routine matcher that connects hair preferences to product use.
projects.intro: Root Ritual is a botanical hair-care brand organised around everyday finishing, pre-wash scalp care and lightweight care for ends. I designed and built its product-discovery website, pairing a three-product collection with an interactive routine matcher.
projects.customer: Hair-care shoppers comparing product purposes and deciding where an oil fits into an existing routine.
projects.problem: A product collection needs to explain differences in use, size and routine placement before a shopper can choose.
projects.offer: Everyday Hair Oil, Pre-Wash Scalp Oil and Ends & Shine Oil each have selectable detail views. Hair-feel and care-timing choices produce a matching routine and product link.
projects.model: The brand model shown is a consumer hair-care range discovered through product education. The delivered website covers discovery rather than transactions.
projects.goal: Make each product purpose clear and connect the collection to a simple care routine.
projects.work: I developed a centred botanical product campaign, an open three-oil collection, detailed product states and preference-based routine matching in JavaScript.
projects.solution: A collection-first boutique layout leads from the central bottle campaign into product comparison and a matching care routine; ingredient information reads as a botanical notebook.
projects.outcome: Three working product views and a routine matcher with nine preference combinations. Product formulas and usage copy are illustrative; no checkout is implemented.
projects.identity: Botanical specimen labels, restrained olive and copper accents and fine beauty typography give the collection a coherent shelf and website identity.
missing: Provide approved product names, formulations, sizes and usage claims before publishing the collection as an actual manufactured range.
Confirm the selling model, prices and fulfilment or checkout scope before claiming a live store.
projects.hero: Hair oils for everyday finishing, pre-wash care and lighter ends. Explore the collection and match a product to your care routine.
projects.perception: Beauty slogans and repeated concept wording overshadow the useful product comparison and matching system.
projects.edits: Name the three oils and their use cases. Replace concept labels with Product details. Explain nine routine combinations and preserve illustrative formula and no-checkout qualifications.

projects.name: The Sunday Table
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A restaurant website with seasonal menu filters, a pickup basket and a sharing-menu plan for two.
projects.intro: The Sunday Table is a neighbourhood restaurant brand centred on seasonal plates and shared meals. I designed and developed a website that joins menu discovery, dietary filtering, meal planning and a local pickup basket.
projects.customer: Diners planning a shared meal and people choosing dishes for collection.
projects.problem: Diners need to compare dishes, dietary information, quantities and estimated spend before deciding what to order.
projects.offer: Dinner, lunch and drinks views, a meat-and-fish filter, item quantities and totals, a four-dish sharing plan and date-based table-time suggestions.
projects.model: The restaurant model shown combines dine-in meals with collection. The website supports menu and visit planning without sending reservations or orders.
projects.goal: Help diners plan a meal and understand their choices before contacting a restaurant.
projects.work: I created the bistro identity and responsive menu, implemented dietary/category filters and built the basket, quantity controls, totals and table-time suggestions.
projects.solution: Browsing, dietary preferences and quantities stay connected, so the basket reflects the meal a visitor has chosen.
projects.outcome: A working menu and basket with changing quantities and totals, plus meal and table-time planning. No order or table reservation is submitted.
projects.identity: Tomato red, printed menu rows, gingham details and sociable language give the restaurant a distinct neighbourhood character.
missing: Provide the real restaurant location, opening hours, approved menu, prices and allergen information before representing a live dining service.
Confirm how a pickup order or table request reaches staff before claiming online ordering or booking.
projects.hero: Seasonal plates for lunch, dinner and sharing. Browse the menu, filter your choices and put together a meal for the table or collection.
projects.perception: The restaurant reads as an attractive preview, while its menu, basket and planning capabilities receive too little explanation.
projects.edits: Lead with seasonal dining and meal planning. Replace Book or Reserve a table with Plan a table. Keep the meat-and-fish filter precise and distinguish the local basket from an order.

projects.name: Good Form Barbers
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A barbershop website connecting five grooming services, barber profiles, a visit planner and practical aftercare.
projects.intro: Good Form Barbers is a barbershop brand built around tailored cuts, beard care and time in the chair. I designed and developed a service-led website that helps visitors compare treatments, plan a visit and find relevant aftercare.
projects.customer: People choosing a haircut or beard service and comparing the time, price and style of a visit.
projects.problem: Visitors need enough service detail to choose a treatment and understand the visit before committing to an appointment.
projects.offer: Five service descriptions, three barber profiles, a service/barber/day/time planner and a style-specific aftercare selector.
projects.model: The service model shown is appointment-based grooming with defined durations and sample prices.
projects.goal: Make service selection clear and reduce the information needed to plan a visit.
projects.work: I built the charcoal and rose visual system, responsive service layouts, visit summary and short-cut, beard and longer-texture aftercare states.
projects.solution: Service, barber and time choices update one visit summary, while aftercare extends the customer journey beyond the selection.
projects.outcome: A working visit planner and three aftercare guides. The planner displays sample appointments and does not request or reserve a slot.
projects.identity: Geometric typography, precise service rails and charcoal with rose accents position the brand around careful craft.
missing: Confirm the operating shop, real team, address, service prices and opening times before these are treated as business facts.
Confirm any booking integration and cancellation/deposit terms before claiming appointment fulfilment.
projects.hero: Tailored haircuts, beard care and finishing details. Compare services, plan time in the chair and find aftercare for your style.
projects.perception: The site has a strong shop personality, but repeated preview labels obscure the complete service-selection workflow.
projects.edits: Lead with five grooming services and the visit planner. Replace Appointments with Appointment planning; retain sample team, prices and slots. Describe three aftercare states without claiming a booking.

projects.name: Kindred Vet
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A veterinary website helping pet owners choose a visit reason, prepare questions and download a private visit note.
projects.intro: Kindred Vet is a veterinary practice brand focused on clear guidance and calmer visits for pets and their owners. I designed and built a website that explains care categories and helps owners prepare a visit note they can take to a veterinary team.
projects.customer: Pet owners organising routine care, preventive visits or questions about a new concern.
projects.problem: Owners need to understand the next step and collect relevant questions and observations before a veterinary conversation.
projects.offer: Pet-species and visit-reason selectors, preparation guidance, service categories, common questions and a downloadable text note for observations, medicines and questions.
projects.model: The practice model shown is appointment-based veterinary care. The delivered product supports visit preparation and information organisation.
projects.goal: Help owners arrive with clear observations and questions, supporting a more organised conversation.
projects.work: I developed a compact care-planning portal, species/reason guidance, service-information panels and private note creation with text-file download.
projects.solution: The pet and visit-reason choices are available immediately, with preparation guidance beside them. A notebook-style form keeps observations and questions in the current tab until the owner chooses to download them.
projects.outcome: A working guidance selector and downloadable visit note. The website does not book visits, diagnose conditions or transmit clinical records.
projects.identity: Rounded typography, pet illustrations, sky and apricot colours and plain-language care guidance create an approachable practice identity.
missing: Provide the real practice, clinicians, approved services, contact details and hours before describing an operating clinic.
Confirm clinical review of care copy and any actual appointment or patient-record integration before expanding those claims.
projects.hero: Care information for pets and the people who know them best. Choose a visit reason and prepare a note with observations and questions for your veterinary team.
projects.perception: Friendly care language communicates tone, but does not clearly identify the practical visit-preparation product or the delivered work.
projects.edits: Lead with visit preparation, species/reason guidance and the downloadable text note. Keep the note local and preserve urgent-care guidance; do not imply clinical diagnosis or appointment submission.

projects.name: Honest Grain
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A furniture website turning piece, size, wood and finish choices into a copyable design brief.
projects.intro: Honest Grain is a furniture brand organised around material choice, useful proportions and custom pieces. I designed and built a website that connects product specifications with a configurator and a clear brief for a prospective commission.
projects.customer: People considering furniture for a space and comparing dimensions, material and finish.
projects.problem: Custom-furniture enquiries need a clear specification before a maker can discuss feasibility and price.
projects.offer: Three furniture pieces, dimension controls, material and finish choices, specification updates and a copyable design brief.
projects.model: The maker model shown is made-to-order furniture discussed through a project brief. The build prepares that brief without submitting an order or quote request.
projects.goal: Turn product interest into a clear specification for a commissioning conversation.
projects.work: I created the measured furniture identity, product/specification views, dimension constraints and configurator, including clipboard copying and an availability message when copying is unavailable.
projects.solution: The configurator keeps the chosen piece and its options together, then translates them into a concise brief the visitor can reuse.
projects.outcome: A working three-piece configurator and clipboard-copy action. Specifications stay visible if copying is unavailable. No quote, manufacturing order or request is sent.
projects.identity: Walnut studies, measured specimen layouts, upright serif typography and monospaced specifications give the brand a workshop vocabulary.
missing: Provide the real maker, product specifications, materials, production constraints and lead times before presenting manufactured products.
Confirm quotation, pricing and request-submission processes before claiming an operating commission service.
projects.hero: Furniture shaped around your space. Explore pieces, choose dimensions and finishes, then prepare a brief for a custom commission.
projects.perception: The craft narrative is convincing, but the portfolio misses the practical handoff from product configuration to a usable brief.
projects.edits: Lead with piece, dimensions, timber and finish choices. Explain the copied brief and clipboard availability message; preserve example lead times and distinguish configuration from a submitted request.

projects.name: One More Plate
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A community kitchen website with meal-day information, dietary notes and a volunteer plan filtered by day and role.
projects.intro: One More Plate is a community kitchen brand bringing shared meals and volunteer participation into one neighbourhood service. I designed and developed a website that connects a meal schedule with role-based volunteer-shift planning.
projects.customer: Neighbours exploring shared meals and volunteers deciding when and how to help.
projects.problem: People need to see what is happening and match the available kinds of work to their time and interests.
projects.offer: Three meal-day views, dietary notes, six sample shifts, day/role filters and a local volunteer plan.
projects.model: The community model shown is shared meals supported by volunteer prep, cooking, welcome and packing roles. Funding and participation terms are unspecified.
projects.goal: Make meals and opportunities to help easy to find, compare and plan around.
projects.work: I created the noticeboard identity, meal-day selector, shift filters, plan count and add/remove/reset interactions.
projects.solution: Meal information and shift roles are connected in one community journey, while a local plan lets visitors organise their preferred shifts.
projects.outcome: Working meal views and a six-shift filtered planner. Selections stay in the page and do not register a volunteer or reserve a place.
projects.identity: Screenprint-inspired type, taped notices, cobalt, marigold and coral create an approachable community identity.
missing: Provide the real organisation, location, meal schedule, verified ingredient information and volunteer terms before representing an operating kitchen.
Confirm the funding model and real volunteer registration/capacity process before describing those operations.
projects.hero: Shared meals and practical ways to help. Explore the meal schedule and plan volunteer time around prep, cooking, welcoming and packing.
projects.perception: The community voice is strong, but the portfolio does not distinguish a usable local shift plan from actual volunteer registration.
projects.edits: Connect the three meal days with six sample shifts. Describe day/role filters and the session-only plan; replace Good company guaranteed with Volunteer role & time and distinguish planning from registration.

projects.name: Small Hours Theatre
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A theatre website connecting production notes, performance-date selection and an interactive seat-and-price preview.
projects.intro: Small Hours Theatre is an intimate theatre brand centred on its programme and audience experience. I designed and built a website that connects production information, date selection and a seating preview before a theatre visit.
projects.customer: Theatregoers comparing productions and dates and considering where to sit.
projects.problem: Visitors need to understand the show, practical visit details and seat options before choosing a performance.
projects.offer: Three selectable productions update notes and performance options; a 32-seat map supports seat selection and a changing total.
projects.model: The theatre model shown is dated performances with seat-based ticket pricing. The delivered build covers selection and price preview.
projects.goal: Connect interest in a production with a clear performance and seating choice.
projects.work: I developed a programme-first typographic playbill, dated production selector, production notes and a ticket-shaped interactive seat map with selection totals.
projects.solution: The programme opens with three dated productions and a large selected-show poster. Production information leads into a seating preview with ticket prices and selection totals.
projects.outcome: Three working production states and a 32-seat selection preview with totals. Seat choices do not hold inventory, reserve seats or issue tickets.
projects.identity: Graphic show typography, a dark stage-like canvas and poster treatments give the theatre a recognisable performance identity.
missing: Provide confirmed productions, cast, dates, venue and accessibility details before presenting a real season.
Confirm ticket prices, live seat inventory and checkout integration before claiming ticket sales or reservations.
projects.hero: An intimate theatre programme, with stories worth making time for. Explore productions, choose a date and review a seating plan.
projects.perception: The stage identity is memorable, but the case study does not identify the production-to-seat decision flow or the limits of the ticket preview.
projects.edits: Explain the production-to-seat journey. Describe a 32-seat interface rather than a real venue capacity, and keep sample ticket data distinct from seat holds or sales.

projects.name: First Whistle Academy
projects.scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.
projects.card: A youth football academy website helping families compare U7–U16 programmes and prepare for a first session.
projects.intro: First Whistle Academy is a youth football academy brand organised around age-group coaching for U7–U16 players. I designed and built its website to connect programme selection, training information and first-session preparation in one clear journey.
projects.customer: Parents and guardians comparing training options, and young players preparing to join an age-appropriate group.
projects.problem: Families need to understand the coaching focus, session format and practical preparation before choosing a programme.
projects.offer: Three age-group views show coaching priorities, session length and sample schedules. A kit checklist and first-session guide turn interest into practical preparation.
projects.model: The academy model shown is scheduled age-group coaching, supported by programme information and an introductory session journey.
projects.goal: Help families identify the right programme and arrive prepared for a first session.
projects.work: I created the athletic website identity, responsive page structure, age-group selector, changing programme details and interactive kit checklist.
projects.solution: Programme content follows the family decision process: choose an age group, understand the training, then prepare for the first visit.
projects.outcome: A responsive website with three working programme states and a four-item checklist. Enrolment and trial booking are outside the delivered scope.
projects.identity: Condensed athletic type, navy and chartreuse, tactical pitch graphics and direct coaching language give the academy a recognisable identity.
missing: Confirm whether this brand represents an operating academy, and supply its approved location, programmes and session schedule before presenting these as live services.
Supply trial/enrolment terms and pricing if the case study is to describe a confirmed commercial offer.
projects.hero: Youth football programmes for U7–U16 players. Compare age groups, understand the training and prepare for a first session.
projects.perception: The athletic identity is developed, but the portfolio presents a preview without explaining the academy offer or my delivered scope.
projects.edits: Lead with the U7–U16 training offer, then show programme selection and the kit checklist. Replace Sport & Membership with Programme discovery; retain sample schedules and distinguish preparation from enrolment.

projects.name: InfraLock
projects.card: An IP intelligence system connecting a Rust lookup service with a Next.js interface for geolocation and network-risk signals.
projects.intro: InfraLock brings IP geolocation, VPN and proxy signals into a web lookup experience. My work connects a Rust lookup service with a Next.js interface so network information can be reviewed in one place.
projects.customer: Application developers and technical users evaluating IP information.
projects.problem: IP information needs both a lookup system and a readable interface before it is useful in a technical workflow.
projects.offer: A Rust lookup service and Next.js interface presenting IP geolocation, VPN/proxy information and threat signals.
projects.model: A technical lookup service accessed through a web interface.
projects.goal: Make IP lookup data accessible through a clear web interface.
projects.work: I developed the Rust lookup service and its connection to the Next.js interface.
projects.solution: The service performs the lookup and the interface presents the resulting network context.
projects.outcome: A Rust lookup service connected to a Next.js interface for reviewing IP geolocation and network-risk signals.
projects.scope: Earlier software project with a linked repository; production deployment is not documented.
missing: Confirm current release status, implemented threat signals and any commercial API terms before describing a live service.
projects.identity: The product category and documented technical work provide the positioning.
projects.perception: The existing copy foregrounds learning or exploration and leaves the product purpose, my contribution and delivery status implicit.

projects.intro: Livepair is a web application for sharing coding sessions live. I developed the application with Next.js, Node.js, Express and MongoDB, connecting the broadcast experience with an application backend.
projects.customer: Developers sharing a coding session and viewers following the work.
projects.problem: A coding session needs a live sharing interface that keeps the focus on the work being shown.
projects.offer: A live code broadcasting application with a Next.js interface and Node.js, Express and MongoDB stack.
projects.model: A focused web application for live sharing of coding sessions.
projects.goal: Provide a focused way to share a coding session live.
projects.work: I developed the application interface and backend using Next.js, Node.js, Express and MongoDB.
projects.solution: The web interface and application backend support the live code-broadcasting experience.
projects.outcome: A live code-broadcasting application with an application backend. The repository remains private while the product is refined.

projects.name: Lunge
projects.card: A fitness app combining workouts, food logging, daily goals and progress statistics, with AI-assisted planning and social features.
projects.intro: Lunge is a React Native and Expo fitness application for organising workouts, tracking food and reviewing progress. I developed the mobile experience across planning, logging, goals and social workflows, with AI-assisted plans and support for seven languages.
projects.customer: People planning workouts and recording activity and nutrition over time.
projects.problem: Training, food intake and progress are easier to review when the records are connected in one application.
projects.offer: Workout planning and logging, food records, goals and progress statistics, plus AI-assisted plans, moderation, social functionality and seven languages.
projects.model: A mobile product with connected planning, logging and progress workflows.
projects.goal: Connect everyday fitness records with an understandable view of personal progress.
projects.work: I developed the React Native and Expo application over a year, connecting workout, food, goal, progress and social workflows.
projects.solution: The app brings planning, logging, goals and progress views into one mobile experience.
projects.outcome: A mobile fitness product bringing workout and food records together with goals, progress views and the documented social and AI-assisted features.
projects.scope: Earlier mobile and full-stack product work; current availability requires confirmation.
missing: Confirm the current release/distribution and which AI and social capabilities are shipped before describing availability.
Provide the pricing model if a commercial fitness product is to be claimed.

projects.goal: Present a service business clearly in a responsive website.
projects.work: Page structure, frontend implementation and responsive visual design.

projects.name: Algorithmic Research
projects.card: Python research in cryptocurrency data analysis, backtesting and risk models for evaluating trading algorithms.
projects.intro: Algorithmic Research is my Python work on data analysis, backtesting and risk models, using cryptocurrency markets as a test environment. I build research tools to examine how an algorithm behaves under explicit assumptions.
projects.customer: Developers evaluating trading strategies, data assumptions and risk behaviour.
projects.problem: Algorithmic ideas need a structured way to examine behaviour against data and risk assumptions.
projects.offer: Python tools for data analysis, backtesting and risk modelling.
projects.model: An independent research workflow built around Python analysis and strategy evaluation.
projects.goal: Make trading ideas testable and examine the assumptions behind their behaviour.
projects.work: Python research and system development across data analysis, backtesting and risk modelling.
projects.solution: Data and explicit evaluation rules turn an idea into something that can be examined systematically.
projects.outcome: Python research tools for examining market data, testing algorithms and evaluating risk assumptions.

missing: Provide datasets, evaluation methodology, transaction-cost assumptions and reproducible results before publishing performance claims.

projects.name: Interface Interaction Study
projects.card: An interactive interface study comparing typography, spatial rhythm and motion across three visual states.
projects.intro: The Interface Interaction Study examines how typography, spatial rhythm and motion change the character of one screen. I designed and implemented three selectable states, with clear selection feedback and reduced-motion behaviour.
projects.customer: Visitors and designers comparing interface decisions.
projects.problem: A visual direction is easier to explain when its effects can be inspected through a working screen.
projects.offer: Type, Rhythm and Motion states switched by three buttons, with selected-state feedback and changing descriptive text.
projects.model: An independent interface study supporting design comparison rather than a company or commercial service.
projects.goal: Make three interface decisions visible and comparable.
projects.work: Composition, typography, state styling, button behaviour, aria-pressed selection feedback and reduced-motion support.
projects.solution: The same screen changes state so visitors can compare its hierarchy, balance and response.
projects.outcome: A working comparison of three interface states. No usability study or conversion result is claimed.
projects.identity: A graphic studio composition provides a consistent screen across the three treatments.
projects.scope: Independent interface study; decorative Index, About and command-key labels are not working navigation.
projects.perception: The study is described as an original concept and leaves its actual state-switching behaviour unexplained.
projects.unclear: The implementation is directly inspectable, but the original copy leaves the three design decisions and their visible effects unexplained. No usability evaluation is documented.
projects.edits: Describe the Type, Rhythm and Motion states literally. Keep the independent study identity visible on mobile. Do not imply that decorative Index, About or command-key labels are working controls.
